summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, insulin-dependent diabetes, morbid obesity, and recent cellulitis was readmitted due to recurrent erythema, swelling, and fever in the left lower extremity just days after prior discharge. Imaging revealed subcutaneous gas suggestive of necrotizing fasciitis, prompting emergent surgical debridement. He underwent three procedures: initial debridement, a washout with wound vac placement, and a second debridement for progressive tissue involvement. Cultures were negative, likely due to prior antibiotics. He was managed with vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, and clindamycin (later discontinued), along with insulin for glucose control. His infection resolved, white count normalized, and he transitioned to oral intake and ambulation. He was discharged to a rehabilitation facility on continued IV antibiotics with plans for follow-up in infectious disease and surgery clinics.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
